descriptionChirho: The numeral ten thousand or myriad, a later Aramaizing synonym of רְבָבָה used for large round numbers. All forms (singular רִבּוֹ/רִבּוֹא, plural רִבֹּאוֹת/רִבּוֹת, dual רִבֹּתַיִם, construct רֻבֵּי) express the same basic numeric concept of a very large quantity in units of ten thousand. Attested in census/inventory contexts (1 Chr 29:7; Ezra 2:64; Neh 7:66-72), in Daniel's apocalyptic thousands (Dan 11:12), in Hosea's condemnation of multiplied altars (Hos 8:12), and in the psalmist's praise of God's chariots (Ps 68:17). Arabic عَشْرَةَ آلَافٍ/رَبْوَاتٍ (ten thousand/myriads), Korean 만 (ten thousand), Spanish diez mil/miríadas, Hindi दस हज़ार (ten thousand), French dix mille. The dual form רִבֹּתַיִם in Ps 68:17 means 'twice ten thousand' (= 20,000). The Hos 8:12 textual variant [רבו]/(רֻבֵּי) is the same lexeme with a construct plural meaning 'myriads of.'
